main_body: Snow-roofed stone well: a snow-covered roof on two wooden posts, with a stone well body below that has a dark water opening and a bucket
top_band: At the well body, a grey stone rim with a dark opening ellipse at rows 16-22 (the lid and bucket are brown). The roof above has a white/pale blue snow top at rows 1-7 and a light-blue front edge at rows 8-9.
evidence: Reading down the middle column, the snow roof is a broad light band about 7 rows tall, with a pale blue front edge and icicles. Below it the posts and shaded gap read as set back under the roof. The well mouth is a dark ellipse about 5-6 rows tall inside a stone rim, with a brown bucket or lid visible. Below that is a stone front face of about 8 rows with dark course lines. This matches the reference well: horizontal surface on top, a visible opening, and a vertical front. No receding side faces.

style.evidence: The snow has 4-5 white and blue steps with a scalloped edge and icicles. The wood posts have 3-4 browns, and the stone has a few greys with dark bands. Outlines are tinted brown or blue-grey, not near-black. The lower stone band is a bit flat and banded, so the piece is slightly less rich than the reference well, but it would sit acceptably beside it.
